title: Noise floor & adaptive thresholds exploratory notes
content:
Summary:

This is an exploratory collection of notes, hypotheses, and small experiments around dealing with persistent low-amplitude pager noise (the "noise floor") and automating adaptive alert thresholds to reduce wake-ups while preserving SLO early-warning signal. The goal: reduce pagers triggered by transient jitter or metric sparsity while keeping SREs notified for genuine regressions or sustained SLO burns.

Context / motivation:
- Over the past 6 months we've seen a steady stream of low-priority pages tied to small spikes in 95/99 latencies and infrequent exporter hiccups. These pages are costly (context switching) and desensitize oncall.
- Root causes are often: exporter scrape jitter, downstream dependency flapping for <5 minutes, metric cardinality explosion causing momentary aggregation delays, or sudden short-lived traffic bursts from a bot crawl.
- Existing static thresholds are brittle: either too sensitive (false positives) or too coarse (missed degradations).

Hypotheses to test:
1) An explicit "noise floor" per metric/time-window (baseline + variance) will reduce false positives compared to static thresholds.
2) Dampening alerts by requiring an amplitude above noise floor for two consecutive evaluation windows (or 80% of last N samples) reduces churn without delaying detection beyond acceptable time-to-detect.
3) Adaptive thresholds that incorporate recent seasonal baselines (hour-of-day, day-of-week) will improve precision for metrics with diurnal behavior.
4) Short-lived exporter gaps should not trigger SLO pages if a synthetic heartbeat or persisted cache shows service is healthy.

Small experiments & results so far:
- Experiment A: Rolling baseline with quantile smoothing
- Method: compute 30-minute rolling p50/p90/p95 for latency; set alert threshold = max(static_threshold, rolling_p95 + 2 * rolling_stddev)
- Duration: 3 weeks on staging serving-latency clusters
- Result: Pages reduced by ~42% on staging; median time-to-detect for sustained regressions (>=10m) increased by ~30s, still within SLO detection goal.
- Notes: Need to cap window to avoid blind spot during true step-change regressions; add emergency override if absolute token error rate rises.

- Experiment B: Consecutive-window dampening
- Method: require metric to exceed adaptive threshold in 2 of 3 consecutive 1m windows before firing.
- Duration: 2 weeks on subset of services (routing, cache-layer)
- Result: Reduced repeated one-off pages from 18/day to 5/day for those services; one incident where a fast degradation crossed threshold but recovered within 90s (no page) — acceptable.

- Experiment C: Metric heartbeat sentinel
- Method: create synthetic heartbeat metric from proxy that reports basic health every 10s; tie alert suppression to heartbeat present.
- Result: Suppressed 11 exporter-gap pages in 10 days. Helps with short-lived exporter flakiness but requires broad exporter integration.

Proposal (short-term implementable steps):
1) Implement per-metric noise floor calculation in Alerting DSL (prototype):
- baseline_window = 30m
- noise_floor = rolling_p50 + alpha * rolling_iqr (alpha = 1.5 initial)
- threshold = max(static_threshold, noise_floor + margin)
- Exemptions: metrics with <X data points per window (sparsity) should fall back to static thresholds.

2) Dampening policy baked into alert evaluation:
- default: require 2 of last 3 evals (1m granularity) to be over threshold for firing.
- aggressive services (payment/auth): 1 of 2 to avoid delay.
- implement as route-level config in alerting service.

3) Heartbeat integration checklist (owner: Maya)
- identify top 30 exporters/services producing noisy pages
- add 10s synthetic heartbeat where missing or ensure agent aggregator persists last-known state for 60s
- add suppression logic: if heartbeat missing, escalate to diagnostic alert channel but do not page SRE immediately; only page if consumed metric SLO is violated for >3m.

4) Seasonalization (next quarter):
- compute hour-of-day and day-of-week baseline offsets for high-variance metrics
- maintain per-service small feature store with diurnal modifiers updated nightly
- use modifiers to shift adaptive threshold; fall back gracefully if insufficient history

Runbook snippets (to add to central runbooks):
- "Noise-floor suspected" triage steps:
 1) Check "metric-heartbeat" for the exporter/ingester. If heartbeat present, treat as high-confidence signal.
 2) Look at raw scrape timings for the exporter (Prometheus target_last_scrape_*). Short jitter? annotate and mute if <90s propagation.
 3) Check dependency graphs: is a downstream (db/cache) showing concurrent small latency bumps? correlate 1m windows.
 4) If false positive: annotate alert with "noise-floor" tag, add to weekly noise review spreadsheet and consider updating alpha/cap for that metric.
 5) If true regression: follow standard SLO incident steps (escalation, mitigation, RCA).

Alert metadata & classification recommendations:
- Add a label "signal_noise_level" with values {low, moderate, high} computed daily for each alerting rule.
- Attach "suppression_reason" when a suppressed alert was observed (e.g., "heartbeat-ok", "within-noise-floor", "consecutive-window-escaped").

Edge cases & risks:
- Risk of masking slow-moving regressions if adaptive baseline drifts with the regression. Mitigation: compute two parallel baselines (short-term and long-term); if both shift upward beyond tolerance, escalate to a different alert route (ops-review) rather than auto-suppressing.
- Cold-start for new services: no historical baseline. Require static thresholds + higher sensitivity for first 72h.
- Cardinality explosions: adaptive baseline might be contaminated. Add cardinality checks and fall back to coarse-grained aggregations.

Monitoring for the experiment success metrics:
- Pager volume delta (daily/weekly) for rules with adaptive thresholds
- Median MTTR for SLO incidents before vs during experiment
- False-positive rate estimated by manual weekly review (sampled alerts)

Implementation notes / TODOs (owners):
- Jordan: prototype noise_floor function in alerting pipeline (PR #1023) — include config knobs for baseline_window, alpha, margin. Target: small canary by 2025-09-22.
- Liam: implement dampening policy as configurable evaluator param and add route mapping. Target: 2025-09-25.
- Maya: heartbeat rollout plan + spreadsheet mapping exporters -> heartbeat status. Target: heartbeat instrumentation for top 30 by 2025-10-05.

Questions for review meeting:
- How long can we safely delay page firing for SRE business across different tiers? (draft proposals: critical=immediate, high=1m dampening allowed, medium=2m)
- What governance for tuning alpha/margin? who owns per-metric overrides?

Open items / experiments to run next:
- Compare noise_floor computed with MAD vs IQR vs standard deviation for robustness to outliers
- Run a blind A/B test for 2 weeks: half rules use static thresholds, half use adaptive+dampening; measure detection lag and false positives
- Add ML-based anomaly scoring for long-tail metrics and route anomalies into "ops-review" rather than immediate page.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep conservative on suppression early — we can be something like "mute but notify" to a lower-severity channel before full suppression.
- Document all suppressed instances automatically to a weekly noise review sheet so product/infra can reprioritize long tail fixes.

Appendix: simple SQL-ish queries for investigation (PromQL-ish pseudo):
- Rolling p95: quantile_over_time(0.95, latency_bucket[30m])
- Noise floor proxy (IQR): p50 + 1.5 * (p75 - p25) over 30m
- Consecutive-window check: sum_over_time((latency > threshold)[3m]) >= 2

End of notes.

Raw discussion thread snippets (copied from weekly noise review):
- "We muted an alert for cache/shard-7 three times last month; underlying cause was intermittent GC spike on a node — fix is medium effort. Might be worth a targeted job to rotate pods vs generic suppression." — Liam
- "If we add seasonalization we should also surface expected bounds in dashboard to reduce oncall guessing." — Jordan
- "Heartbeats helped for scrapers but are noisy if they piggyback on same exporter process — need separate small agent." — Maya
